transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-29T09:30:00-07:00 (PT)
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Amy Liu (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Acme - Head of ML), Marcus Holt (Acme - Platform Eng), Priya Reddy (Acme - Security)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in — review model results, finalize pinning & fallbacks, define next steps for benchmarks and security review.

[00:00] Samir: ok, good morning everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — review last week's evals, recom for model pinning, and fallback/rollback plan. (uh) Amy's going to run through the metrics.
[00:28] Amy: yeah hi all, I pulled together the test set we agreed on — 2k prompts from cart help + search + returns flows, mixed lengths. baseline was redwood/default-3b-v1.2, plus rl-based redwood/rlhf-7b-v1.3, and we ran a couple runs on gpt-4o via the hosted competitor for a quality comparison.
[01:05] Jenna: quick q — when you say quality comparison, is that human eval or automated?
[01:12] Amy: mostly automated BLEU/ROUGE-ish plus a small human spot check, 200 samples. humans flagged hallucination rates lower on the rlhf-7b but latency is ~40% higher.
[01:34] Marcus: what's the latency ballpark? 40% from what baseline?
[01:37] Amy: default-3b avg 220ms p95 in our Dedicated staging profile, rl-7b p95 was 310-330ms on the same infra; cost per 1k tokens roughly 2.6x for rl-7b vs default-3b in our pricing sim. (sorry ballparks)
[02:05] Priya: small sec — are those numbers with KV cache warmed or cold? security wants to see both.
[02:11] Amy: good call — these were mixed; we have separate warm-cache runs where p95 drops by ~30ms for both models, but rl-7b still stays higher. logs are in the shared benchmark sheet. link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-sep (note: doc link)
[02:45] Samir: ok thanks. recommendation from eng side — pin customer-facing high-quality route to redwood/rlhf-7b-v1.3 but create fallback route pinned to redwood/default-3b-v1.2 for timeouts or capacity constraints. Also set an automatic rollback policy to v1.2 if error-rate or latency SLO breached.
[03:12] Jenna: what triggers would that rollback use? is it token-level errors or end-to-end failed outputs?
[03:20] Amy: we propose 3 signals: sustained p95 > 500ms over a 5m window, error-rate increase of >2x baseline, or a quality regression detected by eval probes (we send a weekly probe set).
[03:45] Marcus: can we test automated rollback without touching prod? we want to simulate flapping.
[03:49] Amy: yes, SE can run a canary with simulated failures. I'll run the rollback test in staging and share logs.
[04:05] Samir: also note cost routing — for lower tier customers we can route to default-3b to save money, that's separate from fallback.
[04:18] Jenna: sounds good. a concern from product: are there semantic differences between the models that confuse downstream intent classifiers?
[04:26] Amy: minor differences, we saw a 3% delta in intent accuracy in one set. we can normalize outputs with post-processing for slot-filling routes.
[04:38] Jenna: ok. next, version pinning process — what does pinning look like operationally?
[04:44] Samir: pinning is model-name + artifact hash in the catalog e.g., redwood/rlhf-7b@v1.3-hash. you can pin per-route in the deployment config; rollouts can be canary (10%) -> 50% -> 100% with auto-rollback.
[05:01] Marcus: how easy is rollback? does it spin up different containers or change routing?
[05:06] Amy: routing change — the runtime switches to a pinned variant; we keep both model variants available in the pool during canary, so it's quick. rollback is basically a routing update and we patch metrics.
[05:22] Marcus: any cold start cost?
[05:25] Amy: if the fallback wasn't pre-warmed, yes there is a short spike; recommended approach is to keep fallback pool pre-warmed for critical routes. we'll include warm pool sizing suggestions in the doc.
[05:40] Priya: security check — audit logs and KMS. we need to confirm retention windows for logs and whether model serving metadata is exported to customer KMS.
[05:50] Samir: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; for Hosted we encrypt at rest and provide audit logs with configurable retention up to 7 years on enterprise plan. we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and the audit log spec.
[06:10] Priya: we also need field-level redaction for PII in logs — can you toggle that?
[06:15] Amy: yes, we can obfuscate PII and only log request hash + metadata. we'll capture requirements and confirm feasible retention.
[06:28] Jenna: back to models — what about fallback semantics, are we going to allow mixed responses where we attempt rl-7b and if it times out we call default-3b and stitch?
[06:37] Amy: two patterns: 1) hard fallback — if primary fails return secondary; 2) speculative parallel call where you fire both and select first valid answer, but that doubles token costs. we recommended hard fallback for now.
[06:56] Jenna: ok. cost is a big factor for us; any levers to reduce unit cost on rl-7b?
[07:03] Amy: quantization profiles, smaller context windows, prefix caching and batching — Redwood Optimize gave suggestions: use int8 quant on rl-7b where acceptable, and enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts which reduced tokens by ~12% in our sim.
[07:24] Marcus: can you show the catalog comparison matrix again? the one with quality vs latency vs cost.
[07:29] Amy: sure — (screen share) listing: default-3b-v1.2 (low cost, low latency, moderate quality), rl-7b-v1.3 (high quality, higher latency/cost), plus an experimental quantized rl-7b-q1 (same quality, lower cost but needs validation).
[07:57] Jenna: experimental ones are interesting but we want stability for POC. prefer pinned rl-7b-v1.3 + fallback to default-3b.
[08:07] Samir: acknowledged. we'll pin rl-7b-v1.3 for the "checkout-help" route and default-3b for quick heuristics route.
[08:18] Marcus: on rollbacks, can we have a canary policy that pauses rollout if quality probes dip?
[08:25] Amy: yes that's standard — canary will stop and rollback if probe scores drop below threshold.
[08:31] Jenna: can we get a script to replay production traffic to reproduce the spike we saw last week?
[08:36] Amy: yes Marcus we'll need a sanitized 24h sample. Marcus: are you able to share that?
[08:40] Marcus: yes, we'll deliver a sanitized sample by end of week.
[08:44] Priya: security will run a quick audit on request/response fields.
[08:47] Jenna: ok, other risks?
[08:50] Amy: one important note — the catalog naming can be slightly different in the UI vs API; sometimes tokenization of model names gets mis-transcribed in logs. just to call it out because we've seen restore attempts fail if exact hash not used.
[09:05] Marcus: noted. please include exact catalog name and artifact hash in the config you send.
[09:10] Samir: will do.
[09:15] Amy: quick demo snippet — I'm going to show a rollback simulation: (audio: typing) in staging I forced p95 up and the controller switched routes after 90s, here's the log lines: "route-switch start" -> "route-switch complete". I saved the log file to the shared folder. link: https://redwood.app/logs/acme/rollback-sim-0929
[09:45] Jenna: nice. any false positives?
[09:48] Amy: we tuned the debounce window to avoid flapping, default is 3 consecutive windows of 1m each before action.
[09:58] Marcus: about benchmarking — can we run a dedicated run on Reserved capacity to see production-like results?
[10:03] Samir: yes we can schedule a Reserved/Dedicated window; for the POC we recommend a 4-hour run during off-peak — we'll propose windows.
[10:12] Jenna: timeline question — if we pin now, when can we flip prod?
[10:16] Samir: once Marcus provides the traffic and Priya signs off on security telemetry, we can schedule a canary rollout next week — tentative target: 2026-10-12 for live benchmark and pilot flip.
[10:30] Priya: about audit logs, also need to confirm whether full request bodies are stored. we prefer hashed request bodies only.
[10:36] Amy: yes we can provide hashed bodies; full-body storage is only on Private deployments with specific consent.
[10:44] Jenna: OK sounds good. any final blockers?
[10:47] Marcus: none besides sharing traffic and finalizing SOW/pricing.
[10:52] Samir: action item recap — I'll send pinning config + SOW, Amy will run rollback tests, Marcus will share traffic, Priya confirm security constraints. We'll schedule the dedicated benchmark w/c 2026-10-12.
[11:12] Jenna: thanks everyone.
